title: What If You Stood on a Planet Where It Rains Iron?
subject: WASP-76b exoplanet

scenes.text: What if it rained liquid iron? On one planet, it does.
It's WASP-76b, 640 light-years away. Its star side reaches about 2,400 degrees Celsius.
That heat boils iron into gas. Fierce winds carry the iron vapor around to the night side.
There it's about 1,500 degrees, still hot enough to melt rock, and the vapor condenses into liquid iron.
The planet orbits its star in under two days, one face always turned to the fire.
So the iron falls where the dark begins. Astronomers saw it by its fingerprint in the light.

description:
What if you stood on a planet where it rains iron?
WASP-76b reaches about 2,400 C on its day side, and iron vapor condenses into rain on the night side.
